title: A Late Pupil
summary: You are beginning an English lesson in a primary school. Some pupils are still talking, and later a student arrives late. You need to manage the classroom calmly and keep the lesson moving.

steps.title: Getting Attention
opening: It is 9:00 a.m. You have greeted the class.
Most pupils are looking towards you, but a few are still talking. Alex and Maria are having a quiet conversation at the back of the classroom.
You want to politely ask the pupils to stop talking so the lesson can begin.
steps.question: What would you say?

choices.text: We won't start until everyone is quiet.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: Several pupils stop talking immediately.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: Alex and Maria lower their voices, but continue their conversation for a moment.

choices.feedback: Establishes a boundary but is less polite as an initial request.

choices.text: It's time to begin, please stop talking.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: Most pupils stop talking and look towards you.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: Alex and Maria begin putting their things away, but exchange a few more words.

choices.feedback: Polite and clear request to stop talking.

choices.text: I think we can start now.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: Some pupils turn towards the board.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: Alex and Maria continue their conversation, apparently not realising that you want to begin.

choices.feedback: Does not explicitly ask the remaining pupils to stop talking.

transition: Most of the class is now quiet. However, Alex and Maria are still whispering to each other.
You decide to address the remaining conversation before beginning the lesson.

steps.title: Managing the Class
opening: The other pupils are waiting quietly. Alex and Maria are still talking at the back.
You have already signalled that the lesson is about to begin. Now you want to make it clear that everyone needs to stop talking before you start.
steps.question: What would you say?

choices.text: I'm waiting for you to be quiet.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: Alex notices that you are looking towards the back of the classroom.

reaction.speaker: alex
reaction.text: Sorry, teacher.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: He and Maria stop talking and face the front.

choices.feedback: Gets attention, though the instruction could be more explicit.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: Most pupils look towards the board.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: Alex and Maria continue whispering for a few seconds. Then they notice that everyone else is waiting and stop talking.

choices.feedback: Proposes starting without directly dealing with the remaining conversation.

choices.text: We won't start until everyone is quiet.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: Alex and Maria stop talking.

reaction.speaker: maria
reaction.text: Sorry, teacher.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: They turn towards the front. The classroom becomes quiet.

choices.feedback: States a clear expectation after the first signal has not worked.

transition: Everyone is now paying attention. You begin the lesson.
The first ten minutes pass normally. The pupils are following the activity when the classroom door opens.

steps.title: A Late Arrival
opening: Anton enters the classroom about ten minutes late. He looks a little embarrassed and stops near the door.
The class notices him, but most pupils remain focused on the lesson.
You want to find out why he is late without making him unnecessarily uncomfortable.
steps.question: What would you say?

reaction.speaker: anton
reaction.text: No, teacher. I missed my bus.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: Anton looks down for a moment, waiting for your response.

choices.feedback: Presumes a cause and can embarrass the pupil.

reaction.speaker: anton
reaction.text: Sorry I'm late. I missed my bus.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: Anton explains the situation and waits quietly.

choices.feedback: Asks for an explanation without presuming the reason; tone still matters.

choices.text: We started ten minutes ago. What have you been doing?

reaction.speaker: anton
reaction.text: Sorry, teacher. I missed my bus.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: He seems a little uncomfortable being questioned in front of the class.

choices.feedback: Requests an explanation, but the phrasing is more confrontational.

transition: You acknowledge Anton's explanation and let him take his seat.
Anton sits down quietly and takes out his notebook. The other pupils are waiting for the lesson to continue.

steps.title: Returning to Work
opening: Anton has taken his seat. The interruption is over, and everyone is paying attention.
You want to return to the learning activity without spending more time discussing the late arrival.
steps.question: What would you say?

reaction.speaker: anton
reaction.text: Okay, teacher.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: Anton looks back at his notebook. The other pupils wait for you to continue.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: You turn towards the board.

choices.feedback: Continues focusing on the late arrival instead of returning to work.

choices.text: Now we can get down to work.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: The pupils turn their attention back to the activity.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: Anton opens his notebook and joins the rest of the class.

choices.feedback: Directs attention back to the activity.

choices.text: I think we can start now.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: The pupils look towards you.

reaction.speaker: narrator
reaction.text: Although the lesson has already started, they understand that it is time to continue working.

choices.feedback: Communicates a transition but inaccurately suggests the lesson has not yet started.

final: You continue the English lesson. Anton follows the activity with the other pupils.
The classroom returns to its normal routine.
